layers.scope: Defines how the system is observed in operation: instrumentation and telemetry configuration, metrics, spans and traces, logs, alerts, dashboards and service-level objectives, with the resources and attributes that describe them (OpenTelemetry 1.0). Logging, metrics and tracing code, exporters and alerting rules are evidence for elements here. Modelling rules: a resource identifies the producing entity: it aggregates the instrumentation scopes running in it, maps to the application component it describes and references its node and system software. A scope aggregates the spans, metric instruments and log records emitted under it, which inherit the resource through it; a span composes its events and aggregates its links. Trace, metric and log configurations (providers) depend on the resource they are built with and aggregate their processors and exporters; they configure telemetry and do not emit, serve or monitor it. An instrumentation configuration monitors the library or code it instruments and references the scope it emits under. Each signal flows through its own processors to exporters, and an exporter accesses the storage it writes to and is served by the technology service it sends to; signals of different kinds are correlated by references (a log record to its span, a metric's exemplars to spans, a span link to its span), not by flow. Only signals and instrumentation configurations monitor elements in other layers; alerts and dashboards monitor signals, and a dashboard references the alerts it shows. Telemetry reaches the business layer only through business KPIs, metric instruments that monitor business processes and services; a metric that tracks an outcome measures it, and telemetry satisfies requirements and constraints.

types.title: Alert
types.description: A declarative rule configured in a monitoring backend that evaluates a threshold or query expression over telemetry (metrics, spans, logs) at a recurring interval and sends a notification to one or more destinations when the expression holds. It is the persisted rule definition, not a single firing or incident instance. Use Dashboard instead when the artifact only visualizes signals in panels and has no triggering condition or notification routing of its own. Use MetricInstrument instead when the symbol defines the measured quantity itself (a Counter, Histogram or Gauge created via a Meter) rather than a rule that evaluates that quantity. Use LogRecord instead when the thing is a single emitted event or log entry, including a record of an alert having fired, rather than the standing rule that decides when to fire. Use LogConfiguration instead when the severity threshold only filters which log records the SDK emits, rather than triggering a notification when a condition over signals is met.
evidence: A Prometheus rules YAML file with a groups[].rules[] entry that has an 'alert:' name, an 'expr:' PromQL condition, an optional 'for:' duration and a 'labels.severity' value

An infrastructure-as-code resource such as Terraform 'datadog_monitor', 'grafana_rule_group', 'newrelic_alert_condition' or 'aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm' (or CloudFormation AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm) that declares a query or threshold and notification targets
An Alertmanager or Grafana contact-point/route configuration, or a monitor JSON export, that binds a named rule to Slack, PagerDuty or email receivers

distinguish.apm.dashboard: the artifact only visualizes signals in panels and has no triggering condition or notification routing of its own
distinguish.apm.metricinstrument: the symbol defines the measured quantity itself (a Counter, Histogram or Gauge created via a Meter) rather than a rule that evaluates that quantity
distinguish.apm.logrecord: the thing is a single emitted event or log entry, including a record of an alert having fired, rather than the standing rule that decides when to fire
distinguish.apm.logconfiguration: the severity threshold only filters which log records the SDK emits, rather than triggering a notification when a condition over signals is met

types.title: Dashboard
types.description: A persisted monitoring-platform view definition that arranges one or more visualization panels, each querying metrics, traces, logs or alert state, into a single named page for human inspection. It is the definition of the view (e.g., Grafana dashboard JSON, Datadog dashboard resource), not the underlying signals or the queries' alerting logic. Use Alert instead when the artifact evaluates a condition on a schedule and sends notifications, even if it is defined in the same platform or shown on a dashboard panel. Use MetricInstrument instead when the code creates or records a measurement (Counter, Histogram, Gauge) rather than displaying or querying one. Use ExporterConfig instead when the configuration sends telemetry to a backend (endpoint, protocol, auth) rather than defining how that backend visualizes it.
evidence: a Grafana dashboard JSON file (with 'panels', 'targets' and 'templating' keys) under a dashboards/ or provisioning/ directory, or a grafana-dashboard ConfigMap in Kubernetes manifests
an infrastructure-as-code resource such as Terraform 'datadog_dashboard', 'grafana_dashboard', 'aws_cloudwatch_dashboard' or 'newrelic_one_dashboard' containing widget definitions
a dashboard-as-code module (e.g., grafonnet/Jsonnet, grafanalib Python, CDK Dashboard construct) that builds panels with PromQL, LogQL or trace queries

distinguish.apm.alert: the artifact evaluates a condition on a schedule and sends notifications, even if it is defined in the same platform or shown on a dashboard panel.
distinguish.apm.metricinstrument: the code creates or records a measurement (Counter, Histogram, Gauge) rather than displaying or querying one.
distinguish.apm.exporterconfig: the configuration sends telemetry to a backend (endpoint, protocol, auth) rather than defining how that backend visualizes it.

types.title: ExporterConfig
types.description: A telemetry export configuration that binds one OpenTelemetry exporter (SpanExporter, MetricExporter/pull reader, or LogRecordExporter, or an OTel Collector exporter) to a concrete destination, specifying the exporter kind, endpoint, wire protocol, authentication and compression used to send or expose observability data outside the process. Use LogProcessor instead when the element filters, enriches, batches or routes log records before they reach an exporter, rather than defining the destination and transport itself. Use TraceConfiguration instead when the element is the TracerProvider setup (sampler, propagators, span processor pipeline) that merely registers an exporter, not the exporter's endpoint and transport settings. Use MetricConfiguration instead when the element sets MeterProvider-wide behaviour such as export interval, timeout, cardinality limits or exemplar filtering, rather than where and how metrics are delivered. Use LogConfiguration instead when the element configures the LoggerProvider pipeline and minimum severity, with the exporter only wired in as a component.
evidence: Instantiation of an exporter class with destination options, e.g. new OTLPTraceExporter({ url, headers }), OTLPMetricExporter, JaegerExporter, ZipkinExporter, PrometheusExporter({ port }), or ConsoleSpanExporter.

Environment or deployment variables such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_COMPRESSION or OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER in .env files, Helm values or Kubernetes manifests.
An 'exporters:' block in an OpenTelemetry Collector YAML config (e.g. otlp, otlphttp, prometheus, debug) with endpoint, tls and headers keys, referenced from a service pipeline.

distinguish.apm.logprocessor: the element filters, enriches, batches or routes log records before they reach an exporter, rather than defining the destination and transport itself.
distinguish.apm.traceconfiguration: the element is the TracerProvider setup (sampler, propagators, span processor pipeline) that merely registers an exporter, not the exporter's endpoint and transport settings.
distinguish.apm.metricconfiguration: the element sets MeterProvider-wide behaviour such as export interval, timeout, cardinality limits or exemplar filtering, rather than where and how metrics are delivered.
distinguish.apm.logconfiguration: the element configures the LoggerProvider pipeline and minimum severity, with the exporter only wired in as a component.

types.title: InstrumentationConfig
types.description: A telemetry configuration entry that selects one instrumented library, framework or application code path and sets whether and how it is instrumented. This covers an auto-instrumentation plugin registered at SDK bootstrap, or a manual instrumentation site using the OTel Tracer/Meter/Logger API. It does not cover where telemetry is sent, how it is sampled, or which individual instruments are defined. Use InstrumentationScope instead when the element is the name/version/schemaUrl identity stamped on emitted telemetry (the tracer or meter name), not the setting that turns instrumentation of a library on or off. Use TraceConfiguration instead when the configuration governs TracerProvider-wide behaviour such as sampler, propagators or span processor pipeline rather than which library or code path is instrumented. Use ExporterConfig instead when the configuration specifies the destination, protocol, endpoint, authentication or compression for exported telemetry. Use MetricInstrument instead when the code creates a specific Counter, Histogram or Gauge with its own name and unit; that is an instrument produced by instrumentation, not the instrumentation setting itself.
evidence: A registerInstrumentations([...]) or getNodeAutoInstrumentations({...}) call listing plugins such as '@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http' with per-plugin enabled flags or options

Environment variables or agent flags such as OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_<NAME>_ENABLED, OTEL_NODE_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS, OTEL_PYTHON_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS or -javaagent:opentelemetry-javaagent.jar in a Dockerfile, Helm values or startup script

An opentelemetry-instrumentation-* dependency invoked in code (e.g., FlaskInstrumentor().instrument_app(app)), or a wrapper module that calls trace.getTracer('<lib>') to manually instrument a specific code path

distinguish.apm.instrumentationscope: the element is the name/version/schemaUrl identity stamped on emitted telemetry (the tracer or meter name), not the setting that turns instrumentation of a library on or off
distinguish.apm.traceconfiguration: the configuration governs TracerProvider-wide behaviour such as sampler, propagators or span processor pipeline rather than which library or code path is instrumented
distinguish.apm.exporterconfig: the configuration specifies the destination, protocol, endpoint, authentication or compression for exported telemetry
distinguish.apm.metricinstrument: the code creates a specific Counter, Histogram or Gauge with its own name and unit; that is an instrument produced by instrumentation, not the instrumentation setting itself

types.title: InstrumentationScope
types.description: A named telemetry-producer identity, consisting of a name plus optional version, schema URL and attributes, under which code obtains a Tracer, Meter or Logger so that every span, metric and log record it emits is tagged with that origin. It identifies the instrumenting library or module, not the service or process that runs it. Use Resource instead when the identity describes the service, host, process or deployment that produces telemetry (service.name, host.name) rather than the library or module within it that emits the signals. Use InstrumentationConfig instead when the element is the setting that selects, enables or disables instrumentation of a library or code path, rather than the name/version identity stamped on the emitted telemetry. Use MetricInstrument instead when the element is an individual Counter, Histogram or Gauge created from a Meter, rather than the named Meter scope that owns the instruments. Use TraceConfiguration instead when the element is TracerProvider-wide sampler, propagator or processor configuration rather than a per-library tracer identity.
evidence: Calls such as trace.getTracer('com.example.payments', '1.2.0'), meterProvider.getMeter(name, version, {schemaUrl}) or loggerProvider.getLogger(name) with a literal or constant library/module name

An instrumentation package whose class passes a name and version constant to its base constructor, e.g. super('@opentelemetry/instrumentation-express', VERSION) or InstrumentationScopeInfo.builder(name).setVersion(...)

Exported telemetry or collector config referencing scope identity: OTLP scopeSpans/scopeMetrics/scopeLogs entries with scope.name, or otel.scope.name / otel.library.name labels used in queries and filters

distinguish.apm.resource: the identity describes the service, host, process or deployment that produces telemetry (service.name, host.name) rather than the library or module within it that emits the signals
distinguish.apm.instrumentationconfig: the element is the setting that selects, enables or disables instrumentation of a library or code path, rather than the name/version identity stamped on the emitted telemetry
distinguish.apm.metricinstrument: the element is an individual Counter, Histogram or Gauge created from a Meter, rather than the named Meter scope that owns the instruments
distinguish.apm.traceconfiguration: the element is TracerProvider-wide sampler, propagator or processor configuration rather than a per-library tracer identity

types.title: LogConfiguration
types.description: A provider-level logging SDK configuration that bootstraps the log pipeline for one service: the OTel LoggerProvider, or an equivalent logging-framework root configuration, that registers log record processors and exporters and sets the minimum severity for emitted log records. It covers the pipeline as a whole, not any single processor, exporter or log record. Use LogProcessor instead when the symbol is one processing stage (simple, batch or custom filter/enricher) that is attached to the log pipeline, rather than the provider setup that assembles the pipeline. Use ExporterConfig instead when the symbol only specifies an export destination (endpoint, protocol, auth, compression) that a log, trace or metric pipeline sends data to. Use Resource instead when the symbol defines service identity attributes (service.name, service.version, deployment.environment) that are merged into all signals rather than log-pipeline settings. Use LogRecord instead when the symbol is an individual emitted log event or the structure of one, rather than the configuration governing emission.
evidence: Construction of an OTel LoggerProvider or SdkLoggerProvider builder that chains addLogRecordProcessor(...) calls and is then registered globally, e.g. via set_logger_provider or OpenTelemetrySdk.builder().setLoggerProvider
Environment or SDK config keys such as OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER, OTEL_BLRP_SCHEDULE_DELAY or a 'logger_provider:' block in an OTel declarative config file
A logging framework root configuration, such as logback.xml, log4j2.xml or Python logging.config dictConfig, that sets the root level and attaches an OpenTelemetry appender or handler

distinguish.apm.logprocessor: the symbol is one processing stage (simple, batch or custom filter/enricher) that is attached to the log pipeline, rather than the provider setup that assembles the pipeline
distinguish.apm.exporterconfig: the symbol only specifies an export destination (endpoint, protocol, auth, compression) that a log, trace or metric pipeline sends data to
distinguish.apm.resource: the symbol defines service identity attributes (service.name, service.version, deployment.environment) that are merged into all signals rather than log-pipeline settings
distinguish.apm.logrecord: the symbol is an individual emitted log event or the structure of one, rather than the configuration governing emission

types.title: LogProcessor
types.description: A log-record pipeline stage registered on an OTel LoggerProvider (or in a Collector logs pipeline) that receives each emitted LogRecord and either forwards it to an exporter, synchronously or in buffered batches, or filters, transforms, enriches or redacts it before passing it on. It models one processor in the chain, not the provider-level logging configuration. Use LogConfiguration instead when the element is the LoggerProvider-level setup (service name, minimum severity, the overall processor/exporter wiring) rather than one stage in the processor chain. Use ExporterConfig instead when the element specifies where and how logs are sent (endpoint, protocol, authentication, compression) rather than how records are handled before export. Use LogRecord instead when the element is an individual log event or the structure of emitted log data rather than the component that handles those records. Use TraceConfiguration instead when the pipeline component processes spans (a SpanProcessor) rather than log records.
evidence: a class implementing the OTel LogRecordProcessor interface (onEmit/emit, forceFlush, shutdown), for example a redaction or enrichment processor

instantiation of BatchLogRecordProcessor or SimpleLogRecordProcessor passed to LoggerProvider.addLogRecordProcessor / SdkLoggerProvider.builder().addLogRecordProcessor, or OTEL_BLRP_* environment variables
an entry under processors: (e.g. batch, attributes, filter, transform, redaction) referenced in an OpenTelemetry Collector service.pipelines.logs.processors list

distinguish.apm.logconfiguration: the element is the LoggerProvider-level setup (service name, minimum severity, the overall processor/exporter wiring) rather than one stage in the processor chain
distinguish.apm.exporterconfig: the element specifies where and how logs are sent (endpoint, protocol, authentication, compression) rather than how records are handled before export
distinguish.apm.logrecord: the element is an individual log event or the structure of emitted log data rather than the component that handles those records
distinguish.apm.traceconfiguration: the pipeline component processes spans (a SpanProcessor) rather than log records

types.title: LogRecord
types.description: A structured log event emitted by application or library code through a logging API or the OTel Logs Bridge API. It is identified by a stable message template or event name together with its severity, body and attributes. It models the kind of record a log call site produces, not a transient annotation on a span. Use SpanEvent instead when the occurrence is recorded on an active span via span.addEvent or span.recordException, rather than emitted through a logger as an independent record. Use LogConfiguration instead when the code sets up the LoggerProvider, its exporters or its minimum-severity filtering, rather than emitting a particular log event. Use LogProcessor instead when the code filters, enriches, batches or routes log records in the pipeline instead of producing them. Use MetricInstrument instead when the occurrence is counted or measured as an aggregated numeric time series instead of being recorded as an individual event with a body.
evidence: A structured logger call with a stable message template or event name plus key-value fields, e.g. logger.warn('payment.declined', {orderId, reason}) or log.info().addKeyValue(...)
A direct OTel Logs Bridge API emission such as logger.emit({severityNumber, severityText, body, attributes}) or LogRecordBuilder.setBody(...).emit()
Documented log or audit event catalogs, or constants enumerating log event names and their fields, e.g. AUDIT_USER_LOGIN = 'user.login' referenced from logging calls

distinguish.apm.spanevent: the occurrence is recorded on an active span via span.addEvent or span.recordException, rather than emitted through a logger as an independent record
distinguish.apm.logconfiguration: the code sets up the LoggerProvider, its exporters or its minimum-severity filtering, rather than emitting a particular log event
distinguish.apm.logprocessor: the code filters, enriches, batches or routes log records in the pipeline instead of producing them
distinguish.apm.metricinstrument: the occurrence is counted or measured as an aggregated numeric time series instead of being recorded as an individual event with a body

types.title: MetricConfiguration
types.description: A process-wide OpenTelemetry metrics SDK configuration, applied once at MeterProvider construction, that sets how all metric instruments are collected and exported: the periodic reader's export interval and timeout, per-instrument cardinality limits, and exemplar filtering and reservoir sizing. It configures the metrics pipeline itself, not any individual instrument or export destination. Use MetricInstrument instead when the symbol defines one named measurement (a Counter, Histogram, Gauge, etc. created via meter.createX) with its own unit and description rather than global collection behaviour. Use ExporterConfig instead when the code specifies where metrics are sent (OTLP or Prometheus endpoint, protocol, authentication, compression) rather than how often and how much is collected. Use TraceConfiguration instead when the setup configures a TracerProvider (sampler, propagators, span processors) rather than a MeterProvider and its metric readers. Use InstrumentationConfig instead when the code enables or disables auto/manual instrumentation libraries that emit metrics, rather than configuring the SDK pipeline that collects them.
evidence: Construction of an SDK MeterProvider (e.g. new MeterProvider({ readers: [...], views: [...] }), SdkMeterProvider.builder(), metrics.set_meter_provider(...)) in service bootstrap code

A PeriodicExportingMetricReader or equivalent instantiated with exportIntervalMillis/exportTimeoutMillis options, or env vars OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL, OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT, OTEL_METRICS_EXEMPLAR_FILTER in deployment manifests
A meter_provider section in an OTel declarative configuration YAML file setting readers, cardinality_limits, or exemplar_filter

distinguish.apm.metricinstrument: the symbol defines one named measurement (a Counter, Histogram, Gauge, etc. created via meter.createX) with its own unit and description rather than global collection behaviour.
distinguish.apm.exporterconfig: the code specifies where metrics are sent (OTLP or Prometheus endpoint, protocol, authentication, compression) rather than how often and how much is collected.
distinguish.apm.traceconfiguration: the setup configures a TracerProvider (sampler, propagators, span processors) rather than a MeterProvider and its metric readers.
distinguish.apm.instrumentationconfig: the code enables or disables auto/manual instrumentation libraries that emit metrics, rather than configuring the SDK pipeline that collects them.

types.title: MetricInstrument
types.description: A named OpenTelemetry metric instrument, obtained from a Meter (e.g. createCounter, histogramBuilder) or declared through an equivalent metrics client, that records measurements of one quantity under a fixed instrument kind and unit. It represents the instrument definition, not individual data points, time series, or the views and exports applied to them. Use MetricConfiguration instead when the code sets MeterProvider-wide behaviour such as export interval, cardinality limits, exemplar filtering, or metric readers, rather than declaring a single named instrument. Use InstrumentationConfig instead when the code enables or configures an instrumentation library that emits metrics automatically, and no instrument is declared directly in application code. Use Alert instead when the artifact is a rule or threshold expression evaluated against a metric's values, such as a Prometheus alerting rule over a histogram, rather than the code that records the metric. Use Span instead when the operation is recorded as a timed unit of work in a trace via Tracer.startSpan, rather than aggregated into a counter, gauge, or histogram.
evidence: A Meter factory call such as meter.createCounter('http.server.request.count', { unit: '{request}', description: ... }) or meter.histogramBuilder("db.client.duration").setUnit("ms").build(), assigned to a field or module-level constant.

A metrics-client declaration such as new prometheus.Histogram({ name, help, buckets }), Counter.builder("orders.placed").register(registry) in Micrometer, or a @Timed/@Counted annotation that creates a named instrument.
Registration of an asynchronous callback, for example meter.createObservableGauge('queue.depth').addCallback(result => result.observe(queue.size())) or a registerCallback reading a pool size.

distinguish.apm.metricconfiguration: the code sets MeterProvider-wide behaviour such as export interval, cardinality limits, exemplar filtering, or metric readers, rather than declaring a single named instrument.
distinguish.apm.instrumentationconfig: the code enables or configures an instrumentation library that emits metrics automatically, and no instrument is declared directly in application code.
distinguish.apm.alert: the artifact is a rule or threshold expression evaluated against a metric's values, such as a Prometheus alerting rule over a histogram, rather than the code that records the metric.
distinguish.apm.span: the operation is recorded as a timed unit of work in a trace via Tracer.startSpan, rather than aggregated into a counter, gauge, or histogram.

types.title: Resource
types.description: An immutable set of OpenTelemetry attributes, built once per SDK or process from code, environment variables or resource detectors, that identifies the telemetry-producing entity (service, host, process, container, cloud instance). The SDK attaches it unchanged to every span, metric and log record that the process's providers emit. Use InstrumentationScope instead when the name, version and attributes identify the library or module that created the tracer, meter or logger, rather than the service or process emitting the telemetry. Use TraceConfiguration instead when the code configures TracerProvider behaviour such as samplers, propagators or span processors, even if a Resource object is passed into the same constructor. Use MetricConfiguration instead when the code sets MeterProvider-level export intervals, cardinality limits or exemplar filtering rather than entity identity attributes. Use Span instead when the attributes vary per operation or request (e.g. http.route, db.statement) instead of being constant for the whole process.
evidence: A Resource constructed via Resource.create / resourceFromAttributes / Resource.getDefault().merge(...) with keys such as service.name, service.version or deployment.environment, then passed to a NodeSDK, TracerProvider, MeterProvider or LoggerProvider constructor.
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME or OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES environment variables set in Dockerfiles, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values or .env files.

Resource detectors registered at SDK bootstrap (e.g. envDetector, processDetector, hostDetector, awsEc2Detector, gcpDetector), or an OTel Collector 'resource'/'resourcedetection' processor block in collector YAML.

distinguish.apm.instrumentationscope: the name, version and attributes identify the library or module that created the tracer, meter or logger, rather than the service or process emitting the telemetry.
distinguish.apm.traceconfiguration: the code configures TracerProvider behaviour such as samplers, propagators or span processors, even if a Resource object is passed into the same constructor.
distinguish.apm.metricconfiguration: the code sets MeterProvider-level export intervals, cardinality limits or exemplar filtering rather than entity identity attributes.
distinguish.apm.span: the attributes vary per operation or request (e.g. http.route, db.statement) instead of being constant for the whole process.

types.title: Span
types.description: A named, timed operation instrumented through the OpenTelemetry Tracer API, or emitted by an instrumentation library, that records one unit of work in a distributed trace with a SpanKind, start and end bounds, a status and attributes. The model element is the span as defined at a code location (name, kind, attributes), not one runtime occurrence. Use SpanEvent instead when the code records a point-in-time annotation inside an already-open span (span.addEvent, span.recordException) rather than opening and ending a new timed operation. Use SpanLink instead when the code attaches a non-parent causal reference to a span in another trace or batch (links passed at span start, Link objects) rather than defining the operation itself. Use TraceConfiguration instead when the symbol builds or configures the TracerProvider (sampler, propagators, span processors) rather than starting spans for a specific operation. Use InstrumentationConfig instead when the symbol only enables or registers an instrumentation library or plugin that produces spans, without itself naming a particular span.
evidence: a call such as tracer.startSpan('name'), tracer.startActiveSpan(...) or `with tracer.start_as_current_span("name")` wrapping a block of application logic, followed by span.end()
a method annotated or decorated for tracing (e.g., @WithSpan, @Traced, @tracer.wrap) whose span name and SpanKind are set in the annotation or decorator
calls on a span handle such as span.setAttribute('http.route', ...), span.setStatus({code: ERROR}) or span.updateName(...) that set the span's attributes and status

distinguish.apm.spanevent: the code records a point-in-time annotation inside an already-open span (span.addEvent, span.recordException) rather than opening and ending a new timed operation
distinguish.apm.spanlink: the code attaches a non-parent causal reference to a span in another trace or batch (links passed at span start, Link objects) rather than defining the operation itself
distinguish.apm.traceconfiguration: the symbol builds or configures the TracerProvider (sampler, propagators, span processors) rather than starting spans for a specific operation
distinguish.apm.instrumentationconfig: the symbol only enables or registers an instrumentation library or plugin that produces spans, without itself naming a particular span

types.title: SpanEvent
types.description: A named, timestamped annotation attached to exactly one span and recorded at a single instant within that span's start–end window. It has no duration and no identity of its own, and it describes a notable occurrence such as a caught exception, retry or state transition inside the operation the span covers. Use LogRecord instead when the event is emitted through a Logger or the OTel Events/Logs API as an independent record (even if it carries traceId/spanId for correlation), rather than being added to a span via addEvent/recordException. Use Span instead when the thing being recorded has its own start and end time, its own spanId, or child operations, i.e. it is a unit of work with duration rather than a point-in-time marker inside one. Use SpanLink instead when the annotation points to another span (traceId+spanId) to express causality across traces or batches rather than recording something that happened at a moment within this span.
evidence: calls to span.addEvent(name, attributes) / span.add_event(...) / Span.current().addEvent(...) on an active span
calls to span.recordException(err) / span.record_exception(e), or events named 'exception' carrying exception.type, exception.message and exception.stacktrace attributes
in .NET, Activity.AddEvent(new ActivityEvent("name", tags: ...)), or exported OTLP/Jaeger payloads showing an 'events' (or 'logs') array nested inside a span

distinguish.apm.logrecord: the event is emitted through a Logger or the OTel Events/Logs API as an independent record (even if it carries traceId/spanId for correlation), rather than being added to a span via addEvent/recordException.
distinguish.apm.span: the thing being recorded has its own start and end time, its own spanId, or child operations, i.e. it is a unit of work with duration rather than a point-in-time marker inside one.
distinguish.apm.spanlink: the annotation points to another span (traceId+spanId) to express causality across traces or batches rather than recording something that happened at a moment within this span.

types.title: SpanLink
types.description: A reference attached to a span that identifies another span by its SpanContext (traceId, spanId, traceState) to record a causal relationship that is not parent-child, such as a batch consumer span pointing to each producer span whose message it processes. It is added when the span is created and belongs to the span that carries it. Use Span instead when the element is the timed unit of work itself, or the referenced span is the direct parent, which is expressed through the span's parentSpanId rather than a link. Use SpanEvent instead when the element is a timestamped annotation of something that happened inside the same span (e.g., an exception) and points to no other span.
evidence: a span started with a links option, e.g. tracer.startSpan(name, { links: [{ context: spanCtx, attributes }] }) in JS or start_as_current_span(name, links=[trace.Link(ctx)]) in Python
Java SpanBuilder.addLink(spanContext[, attributes]) calls made before startSpan()
a messaging consumer that extracts propagated trace context from each message header in a batch and passes the extracted contexts as links instead of setting a parent

distinguish.apm.span: the element is the timed unit of work itself, or the referenced span is the direct parent, which is expressed through the span's parentSpanId rather than a link
distinguish.apm.spanevent: the element is a timestamped annotation of something that happened inside the same span (e.g., an exception) and points to no other span

types.title: TraceConfiguration
types.description: A tracing-SDK configuration, one per TracerProvider (usually one per service process), that fixes the sampler and its ratio, the context propagation formats injected into and extracted from carriers, and the span processors and exporters the provider forwards finished spans to. Use Resource instead when the symbol only sets service identity attributes such as service.name, service.version or deployment.environment that are merged into all signals. Use ExporterConfig instead when the symbol defines a single export destination (endpoint, protocol, auth, compression) rather than the provider-level sampling and propagation setup that uses it. Use InstrumentationConfig instead when the symbol selects or enables instrumentation libraries or manual tracer calls rather than configuring the provider those instrumentations emit into. Use MetricConfiguration instead when the symbol configures a MeterProvider (export interval, cardinality, exemplars) rather than a TracerProvider.
evidence: Construction of a NodeTracerProvider, SdkTracerProvider or TracerProvider with a sampler argument such as ParentBased(TraceIdRatioBased(0.1)) or ALWAYS_ON
Calls such as addSpanProcessor(new BatchSpanProcessor(exporter)) or setGlobalTextMapPropagator(new CompositePropagator([W3CTraceContextPropagator, W3CBaggagePropagator]))
Environment variables OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG or OTEL_PROPAGATORS in deployment manifests, or a tracer_provider section in an OTel Collector/SDK declarative config YAML

distinguish.apm.resource: the symbol only sets service identity attributes such as service.name, service.version or deployment.environment that are merged into all signals.
distinguish.apm.exporterconfig: the symbol defines a single export destination (endpoint, protocol, auth, compression) rather than the provider-level sampling and propagation setup that uses it.
distinguish.apm.instrumentationconfig: the symbol selects or enables instrumentation libraries or manual tracer calls rather than configuring the provider those instrumentations emit into.
distinguish.apm.metricconfiguration: the symbol configures a MeterProvider (export interval, cardinality, exemplars) rather than a TracerProvider.

layers.name: Testing Layer
layers.scope: Describes how the system is verified: test strategies and plans, suites and cases, fixtures and test data, mocks and stubs, coverage targets and summaries, and the environments tests run in (IEEE 829-2008 test documentation). Test files, fixtures and test configuration are evidence for elements here; the production code under test belongs to the layer it implements. Modelling rules: each testing type has one composing parent. A test coverage model composes its coverage targets, input space partitions, context variations, environment factors, exclusions and coverage summary; a coverage target composes its target input fields, outcome categories, coverage requirements and test case sketches; a coverage requirement composes its input partition selections; a partition composes its values; a test case sketch composes its input selections. A test case sketch validates the one coverage requirement it exercises and references the context variation and outcome category it combines; each input selection references the partition value it picks. A coverage requirement references the context variations and outcome categories it needs, and reaches partition values only through its selections. A target input field references its partition and the field under test (an API parameter, schema property or UX component), so partitions stay reusable across fields; a selection references the values it picks, and a partition dependency references its trigger value and the partition it affects. Summaries report and never validate: a coverage summary aggregates the per-target summaries, a target coverage summary references its target, and both reference the gaps and exclusions they count. Gaps and exclusions reference the requirement or target they concern, and an exclusion references the gap it waives. Context variations reference the environment factors they fix, and environment factors reference only technology nodes and system software. A coverage target covers the production artifact it names; a test case sketch tests what it exercises, requires the software it runs on and accesses the stores holding its fixture data; the model covers only the application component, UX application or API document it is for. Requirements and summaries reach no other layer. The model carries the plan-level motivation links (it supports goals, satisfies principles, constraints and requirements, and measures outcomes), and test case sketches satisfy the requirements they verify.

types.title: ContextVariation
types.description: A named test-design condition, classified by test type (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory), under which a TestCoverageTarget is to be exercised, optionally bound to a set of EnvironmentFactors that fix the concrete environment for that condition. It names the whole execution context. It does not name a single environmental variable or an input value. Use EnvironmentFactor instead when the element is a single concrete environmental variable and its value (e.g. 'Ubuntu 22.04', 'en-US', 'latency < 100ms'), not a named test context that groups such variables. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states coverage criteria (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) that must be met, possibly across several contexts, rather than defining one context. Use InputSpacePartition instead when the variation is in the data fed to the target (an input field's equivalence classes), not in the type of test or the execution environment. Use OutcomeCategory instead when the element classifies the expected result (success, timeout, validation-error), not the conditions under which the test runs.
evidence: Separate test suites or directories split by test type, such as tests/load, tests/security, tests/smoke, or pytest markers / JUnit @Tag('smoke'|'regression') used to select runs
CI pipeline jobs or matrix entries that run the same targets under named contexts, e.g. a 'load' job invoking k6/JMeter or a 'security' job invoking OWASP ZAP, each with its own environment variables

Test configuration profiles bundling environment settings per context, e.g. playwright.config projects, tox envs, or application-test-load.yml, that set OS, locale, network throttling or dependency versions

distinguish.testing.environmentfactor: the element is a single concrete environmental variable and its value (e.g. 'Ubuntu 22.04', 'en-US', 'latency < 100ms'), not a named test context that groups such variables
distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: the element states coverage criteria (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) that must be met, possibly across several contexts, rather than defining one context
distinguish.testing.inputspacepartition: the variation is in the data fed to the target (an input field's equivalence classes), not in the type of test or the execution environment
distinguish.testing.outcomecategory: the element classifies the expected result (success, timeout, validation-error), not the conditions under which the test runs

types.title: CoverageExclusion
types.description: A recorded governance decision that removes a specific coverage target or coverage requirement from the coverage that must be achieved. It names the excluded item, gives the rationale, states whether the residual risk is accepted, and identifies the accountable approver. It exists only once someone has explicitly decided and signed off on not testing the item, not merely when the item is observed to be untested. Use CoverageGap instead when the missing coverage has been detected (e.g. in a summary report) but no one has yet approved leaving it untested; a gap may later flow into an exclusion. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when specific partition values are carved out of a single requirement's selection as a test-design choice (excludeValues), without a formal waiver, approver or risk acceptance. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states coverage criteria that must be satisfied rather than a sanctioned decision not to satisfy them. Use TestCaseSketch instead when an individual designed test case is being retired (status deprecated) rather than an entire target or requirement being waived from coverage.
evidence: A coverage-tool ignore entry with a justification comment that cites an approval or ticket, such as a `# pragma: no cover` or `/* istanbul ignore next */` line, `omit` in .coveragerc, or `coveragePathIgnorePatterns` in jest.config.
A test-waiver or exclusions file (YAML, JSON or Markdown) listing excluded endpoints, workflows or requirements with fields such as reason, approver and date.

A skipped or disabled test annotation that carries a reason and a waiver reference, such as `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="waived per QA-123, approved by J. Doe")` or `@Disabled("Excluded: risk accepted, see ADR-12")`.

distinguish.testing.coveragegap: the missing coverage has been detected (e.g. in a summary report) but no one has yet approved leaving it untested; a gap may later flow into an exclusion.
distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: specific partition values are carved out of a single requirement's selection as a test-design choice (excludeValues), without a formal waiver, approver or risk acceptance.
distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: the element states coverage criteria that must be satisfied rather than a sanctioned decision not to satisfy them.
distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: an individual designed test case is being retired (status deprecated) rather than an entire target or requirement being waived from coverage.

types.title: CoverageGap
types.description: A recorded finding that a specific coverage requirement or coverage target lacks the implemented or executed tests it needs. It names what is uncovered, how severe the gap is, and where it stands in remediation. It records a shortfall against required coverage, not a deliberate, approved scope decision and not an aggregate metric. Use CoverageExclusion instead when the uncovered item has been formally approved as out of scope, with a rationale, accepted risk and a named approver, rather than merely found to be missing coverage. Use TargetCoverageSummary instead when you are recording counts or percentages of sketches and implemented tests for a target, rather than a specific uncovered requirement that needs action. Use CoverageSummary instead when the artifact aggregates coverage totals across the whole model instead of describing one identified deficit. Use CoverageRequirement instead when you are specifying the criteria that must be met, rather than recording that those criteria are currently unmet.
evidence: Coverage tool output (e.g. lcov, JaCoCo, coverage.py) or a CI gate failure listing files or endpoints below a configured threshold such as `fail_under` or `coverageThreshold`.
Test files carrying skip or todo markers (`@pytest.mark.skip`, `it.todo`, `xit`, `@Disabled`) with a comment or ticket ID explaining that a requirement or partition is not yet tested.
Issue-tracker items or TEST_GAPS / test-report markdown entries labelled 'coverage gap' or 'missing tests', naming an endpoint or requirement ID and a severity.

distinguish.testing.coverageexclusion: the uncovered item has been formally approved as out of scope, with a rationale, accepted risk and a named approver, rather than merely found to be missing coverage
distinguish.testing.targetcoveragesummary: you are recording counts or percentages of sketches and implemented tests for a target, rather than a specific uncovered requirement that needs action
distinguish.testing.coveragesummary: the artifact aggregates coverage totals across the whole model instead of describing one identified deficit
distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: you are specifying the criteria that must be met, rather than recording that those criteria are currently unmet

types.title: CoverageRequirement
types.description: A test design rule attached to one TestCoverageTarget that names a combinatorial or structural coverage criterion (e.g. boundary-values, pairwise, MC/DC) which the target's test cases must satisfy across selected input partitions, context variations and outcome categories. It states what must be exercised. It is not a test case, not the target itself, and not a measured result. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies the endpoint, workflow, component or job that needs testing, rather than the criterion its tests must meet. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element lists which specific values of one InputSpacePartition are included or excluded, rather than the overall coverage strategy that uses those selections. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element is one designed or implemented test case choosing concrete partition values, rather than the rule that a set of such cases must satisfy. Use CoverageGap instead when the element records a measured shortfall against a requirement found during reporting, rather than the requirement itself.
evidence: A combinatorial test model file, such as a PICT .txt model, an allpairs config or a hypothesis/fast-check strategy, scoped to one endpoint or function, that declares parameters and an order or strategy like pairwise.

A parametrized test table (pytest.mark.parametrize, test.each, JUnit @ParameterizedTest/@CsvSource) whose rows enumerate boundary and invalid classes for one target, with a comment or docstring naming the criterion (e.g. 'boundary values for quantity').

A test plan or test design Markdown/YAML entry that states, per feature or endpoint, a required criterion and priority (e.g. 'POST /orders: all-partitions over status × role, must cover validation-error and authorization-error outcomes').

distinguish.testing.testcoveragetarget: the element identifies the endpoint, workflow, component or job that needs testing, rather than the criterion its tests must meet
distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the element lists which specific values of one InputSpacePartition are included or excluded, rather than the overall coverage strategy that uses those selections
distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: the element is one designed or implemented test case choosing concrete partition values, rather than the rule that a set of such cases must satisfy
distinguish.testing.coveragegap: the element records a measured shortfall against a requirement found during reporting, rather than the requirement itself

types.title: CoverageSummary
types.description: A model-wide test summary report record that totals the coverage targets, coverage requirements and test case sketches of exactly one TestCoverageModel at a point in time. Per-target figures are rolled up from the model's TargetCoverageSummary records. Use TargetCoverageSummary instead when the metrics (sketch, implemented and automated counts or a percentage) describe a single TestCoverageTarget rather than the whole model. Use CoverageGap instead when the artifact records one specific shortfall between required and achieved coverage, with a severity and a remediation status, rather than aggregate totals. Use TestCoverageModel instead when the artifact is the coverage specification itself, holding the targets, partitions and requirements, rather than a generated report about it. Use CoverageExclusion instead when the artifact is an approved decision to leave a target or requirement uncovered, rather than a count of what is covered.
evidence: A script or CI job that loads the test coverage model (YAML or JSON) and emits totals of targets, requirements and test cases with a generation timestamp.
A generated report artifact (e.g. coverage-model-summary.json or a Markdown table in docs/testing) that lists overall counts per model and links to per-target summaries.
A test-reporting dashboard or README section that publishes model-level totals of covered features, requirements and designed test cases for a named application.

distinguish.testing.targetcoveragesummary: the metrics (sketch, implemented and automated counts or a percentage) describe a single TestCoverageTarget rather than the whole model.
distinguish.testing.coveragegap: the artifact records one specific shortfall between required and achieved coverage, with a severity and a remediation status, rather than aggregate totals.
distinguish.testing.testcoveragemodel: the artifact is the coverage specification itself, holding the targets, partitions and requirements, rather than a generated report about it.
distinguish.testing.coverageexclusion: the artifact is an approved decision to leave a target or requirement uncovered, rather than a count of what is covered.

types.title: EnvironmentFactor
types.description: A single named environmental condition of a test run (operating system, network characteristic, locale, hardware configuration or dependency version) pinned to a concrete value or constraint and recorded because it changes how tests behave. It describes one factor of the execution environment, not the test type that bundles factors together nor any input supplied to the system under test. Use ContextVariation instead when the thing being modelled is a named test context (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory) that groups several environmental constraints, rather than one variable with one value. Use PartitionValue instead when the value is an equivalence class of an input field passed to the system under test (request parameter, form field, data property), not a property of the runtime environment. Use InputSpacePartition instead when an input dimension is being divided into equivalence classes. Do this even if that dimension is a locale or OS selector. A single fixed environmental setting is not a partition.
evidence: A CI matrix entry pinning an environment axis, such as a GitHub Actions `strategy.matrix` with `os: [ubuntu-22.04, windows-2022]` or `node-version: [18.x, 20.x]`, or a tox/nox env list over Python versions.

Test setup that forces an environmental condition, such as setting `TZ`/`LANG`/`LC_ALL` environment variables, network-throttling or latency-injection config (toxiproxy, tc netem, Playwright `emulateNetworkConditions`), or a docker-compose test service pinned to a specific image tag.

Conditional test guards keyed on the environment, such as `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')`, Jest `testEnvironment`, or an engines/`.nvmrc`/`.tool-versions` file referenced by test configuration.

distinguish.testing.contextvariation: the thing being modelled is a named test context (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory) that groups several environmental constraints, rather than one variable with one value.
distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the value is an equivalence class of an input field passed to the system under test (request parameter, form field, data property), not a property of the runtime environment.
distinguish.testing.inputspacepartition: an input dimension is being divided into equivalence classes. Do this even if that dimension is a locale or OS selector. A single fixed environmental setting is not a partition.

types.title: InputPartitionSelection
types.description: A coverage-scope rule within a CoverageRequirement that names exactly one InputSpacePartition and declares which of its PartitionValues must be exercised. The rule takes one of two forms: an explicit include list, or all values minus an exclude list. It selects equivalence classes and never binds concrete test data. Use InputSelection instead when a single partition value is bound to a concrete test datum for one specific TestCaseSketch, rather than a set of classes being declared in scope for a requirement. Use PartitionValue instead when you are defining the equivalence class itself (its label, constraint and representative value), not choosing which classes to cover. Use PartitionDependency instead when the inclusion or exclusion of values in one field is conditional on a value chosen in another field. Use CoverageRequirement instead when you are stating the overall criterion (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) and priority, rather than the per-partition value subset it draws on.
evidence: A combinatorial test model file (e.g. a PICT .txt or ACTS model) that lists one parameter with only a subset of its defined value classes.
A test-design YAML/JSON block keyed by an input field or partition name, with include/exclude lists or an 'all: true, except: [...]' form.
A parametrized test (pytest.mark.parametrize, it.each, @EnumSource(mode = EXCLUDE)) iterating over one field's enum or equivalence classes, with specific classes deliberately omitted or excluded.

distinguish.testing.inputselection: a single partition value is bound to a concrete test datum for one specific TestCaseSketch, rather than a set of classes being declared in scope for a requirement.
distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: you are defining the equivalence class itself (its label, constraint and representative value), not choosing which classes to cover.
distinguish.testing.partitiondependency: the inclusion or exclusion of values in one field is conditional on a value chosen in another field.
distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: you are stating the overall criterion (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) and priority, rather than the per-partition value subset it draws on.

types.title: InputSelection
types.description: A single input binding inside one TestCaseSketch that assigns, for one partitioned input field, the chosen equivalence class (a PartitionValue) and the exact datum the test will submit for it. It is owned by exactly one test case, so it records the data that one test actually uses rather than a coverage obligation. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element states which partition values a CoverageRequirement obliges tests to exercise (cover/exclude lists), without fixing a concrete datum for any particular test case. Use PartitionValue instead when the element defines an equivalence class itself (label, constraint, category, representative value) independent of any test case that uses it. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element is the whole test case design (status, implementation format, source) that groups several input bindings. Use TargetInputField instead when the element only associates an input field of the target with its InputSpacePartition, without choosing a value for a specific test.
evidence: A row in a parametrized test table (e.g. pytest.mark.parametrize, JUnit @CsvSource, Jest test.each) that supplies a specific literal for one argument, often named or commented after its class, such as 'age=-1  # invalid: negative'
A test-data file (CSV/JSON/YAML) with one column per input field and one row per test case, consumed by a data-driven runner

A fixture or factory call inside a single test that builds a specific value for a request field, e.g. build_user(email='a@b') or a Faker/hypothesis strategy pinned to a boundary such as max length 255

distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the element states which partition values a CoverageRequirement obliges tests to exercise (cover/exclude lists), without fixing a concrete datum for any particular test case
distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the element defines an equivalence class itself (label, constraint, category, representative value) independent of any test case that uses it
distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: the element is the whole test case design (status, implementation format, source) that groups several input bindings
distinguish.testing.targetinputfield: the element only associates an input field of the target with its InputSpacePartition, without choosing a value for a specific test

types.title: InputSpacePartition
types.description: A test-design artifact that divides the value domain of an input (such as an email address, a quantity or a date range) into a named set of equivalence classes (PartitionValues), each grouping values expected to produce the same behaviour under test. It is reusable across every field with that domain: a TargetInputField binds it to each field under test (an API parameter, schema property or UI input). It also states whether the input must be present in test inputs. Use PartitionValue instead when the element is one individual equivalence class (label, constraint, representative value) rather than the whole set of classes for a field. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element chooses which classes of an existing partition a CoverageRequirement must exercise, rather than defining the classes themselves. Use TargetInputField instead when the element only binds a field of a specific TestCoverageTarget to a partition and records its relevance, without enumerating classes. Use PartitionDependency instead when the element expresses a constraint linking a class in one field's partition to the allowed classes of another field.
evidence: a parametrized test table (e.g. pytest.mark.parametrize, JUnit @ParameterizedTest with @MethodSource, Jest test.each) for one input field whose cases carry class ids such as 'valid', 'empty', 'too_long', 'negative'

a test-data module, enum or factory that enumerates named valid/invalid/boundary value groups for a single request parameter or schema property (e.g. EMAIL_CASES = {valid: [...], malformed: [...], null: [...]})

a property-based generator per field built from named sub-strategies (e.g. hypothesis st.one_of(valid_emails(), malformed_emails())), or a test-design document table listing equivalence classes per parameter

distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the element is one individual equivalence class (label, constraint, representative value) rather than the whole set of classes for a field
distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the element chooses which classes of an existing partition a CoverageRequirement must exercise, rather than defining the classes themselves
distinguish.testing.targetinputfield: the element only binds a field of a specific TestCoverageTarget to a partition and records its relevance, without enumerating classes
distinguish.testing.partitiondependency: the element expresses a constraint linking a class in one field's partition to the allowed classes of another field

types.title: OutcomeCategory
types.description: A test-design classification of the observable result a TestCoverageTarget can produce (success, validation error, authorization error, not-found, server error, exception, timeout), stated at the level of result class rather than exact expected value. Coverage requirements must exercise it, and test case sketches are grouped under it. Use PartitionValue instead when the category classifies an input value (e.g. an invalid or null-empty equivalence class) rather than the result the target returns. Use ContextVariation instead when the category describes the test type or execution condition (functional, load, security, regression) under which the target is exercised, not what it returns. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element specifies a particular case with concrete inputs and a specific expected value or assertion, rather than a class of outcomes. Use EnvironmentFactor instead when the element is the environmental condition (e.g. network latency) that provokes an outcome such as a timeout, rather than the outcome itself.
evidence: test describe/context blocks or test names grouped by result class, e.g. 'returns 404 when resource missing', 'rejects unauthorized caller with 403', 'times out after 5s'
parameterized test tables or fixtures with an expected-outcome column (expected_status, expected_error, expectedOutcome) whose values are status classes or error types rather than exact payloads

assertions that check outcome class rather than exact value, e.g. expect(res.status).toBe(400), pytest.raises(ValidationError), assertThrows(AccessDeniedException), or OpenAPI response codes enumerated per operation in test plans

distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the category classifies an input value (e.g. an invalid or null-empty equivalence class) rather than the result the target returns
distinguish.testing.contextvariation: the category describes the test type or execution condition (functional, load, security, regression) under which the target is exercised, not what it returns
distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: the element specifies a particular case with concrete inputs and a specific expected value or assertion, rather than a class of outcomes
distinguish.testing.environmentfactor: the element is the environmental condition (e.g. network latency) that provokes an outcome such as a timeout, rather than the outcome itself

types.title: PartitionDependency
types.description: A cross-field constraint in combinatorial test design stating that when a specific partition value (the trigger) is selected in one InputSpacePartition, the availability of named partition values in another input field is excluded, required, restricted, or re-ranged, so that generated combinations omit invalid inputs. Use PartitionValue instead when the condition bounds a single field's own equivalence class (its constraintExpression) and does not depend on the value chosen for any other field. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the restriction is a per-CoverageRequirement choice of which values of one partition to cover or exclude (coverValues/excludeValues), not a rule that applies whenever another field takes a given value. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are describing the input dimension itself and its presenceRule (including a plain 'conditional' flag), rather than the specific trigger value and affected values that make it conditional. Use CoverageExclusion instead when a target or requirement is deliberately removed from coverage with an approver and accepted risk, rather than a combination being logically invalid.
evidence: A constraint line in a combinatorial test model file, e.g. a PICT/ACTS model containing 'IF [PaymentMethod] = "invoice" THEN [Country] IN {"DE","AT"};'

A parametrized test generator (e.g. pytest_generate_tests, JUnit ArgumentsProvider, itertools.product filter) that drops or skips tuples when one parameter has a specific value and another has a listed value
A property-based test calling assume()/filter() that ties one generated argument's allowed values to another argument's value, e.g. 'assume(not (account_type == "guest" and role == "admin"))'

distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the condition bounds a single field's own equivalence class (its constraintExpression) and does not depend on the value chosen for any other field.
distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the restriction is a per-CoverageRequirement choice of which values of one partition to cover or exclude (coverValues/excludeValues), not a rule that applies whenever another field takes a given value.
distinguish.testing.inputspacepartition: you are describing the input dimension itself and its presenceRule (including a plain 'conditional' flag), rather than the specific trigger value and affected values that make it conditional.
distinguish.testing.coverageexclusion: a target or requirement is deliberately removed from coverage with an approver and accepted risk, rather than a combination being logically invalid.

types.title: PartitionValue
types.description: A single equivalence class or boundary class of one input dimension, owned by exactly one InputSpacePartition. It is defined by a boundary condition and by a representative value that stands for every value in the class during test design. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are modelling the whole input field or dimension and its complete set of classes, rather than one class within it. Use InputSelection instead when you are binding a specific concrete test datum, used by a particular TestCaseSketch, to one of the partition's classes. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when you are stating which classes of a partition a CoverageRequirement must or must not exercise. Use OutcomeCategory instead when the category classifies expected results (success, validation error, timeout) rather than input values.
evidence: A parametrized test table for a single argument whose case ids name input classes, e.g. @pytest.mark.parametrize ids=['valid','empty','too_long','negative'] or a JUnit @ValueSource/@CsvSource grouped by class.

Test data constants or builder functions named after a class of one field and mirroring a schema constraint, e.g. MAX_LEN_BOUNDARY = 255, invalid_email(), or a 'min - 1' value derived from a minimum declared in the OpenAPI or JSON Schema.
A property-based generator restricted to one class of an input, e.g. a Hypothesis strategy such as st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=100) or a fast-check arbitrary filtered by a regex predicate.

distinguish.testing.inputspacepartition: you are modelling the whole input field or dimension and its complete set of classes, rather than one class within it.
distinguish.testing.inputselection: you are binding a specific concrete test datum, used by a particular TestCaseSketch, to one of the partition's classes.
distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: you are stating which classes of a partition a CoverageRequirement must or must not exercise.
distinguish.testing.outcomecategory: the category classifies expected results (success, validation error, timeout) rather than input values.

types.title: TargetCoverageSummary
types.description: A per-target coverage report record that states, for exactly one TestCoverageTarget, the counts of designed, implemented and automated test case sketches and the share of that target's coverage requirements exercised by at least one implemented test. It reports measured status, not required criteria or identified deficits. Use CoverageSummary instead when the record aggregates totals across all targets and requirements of a whole TestCoverageModel rather than metrics for one target. Use CoverageGap instead when the element records a specific uncovered requirement with severity and remediation status, rather than numeric coverage counts. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element specifies the coverage criteria a target must satisfy, rather than reporting how far they are satisfied. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies the endpoint, workflow or component in scope for testing, rather than its coverage metrics.
evidence: A generated coverage report file (e.g. coverage-summary.json, a JUnit/Allure per-endpoint section) keyed by a single endpoint, route or feature ID with counts of planned, implemented and automated tests
A CI script or reporting job that groups test results by target (e.g. by OpenAPI operationId or tag) and computes a percentage of requirements with passing implemented tests
A traceability matrix row or markdown table in test documentation listing one feature/endpoint alongside sketch count, implemented count, automated count and coverage %

distinguish.testing.coveragesummary: the record aggregates totals across all targets and requirements of a whole TestCoverageModel rather than metrics for one target.
distinguish.testing.coveragegap: the element records a specific uncovered requirement with severity and remediation status, rather than numeric coverage counts.
distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: the element specifies the coverage criteria a target must satisfy, rather than reporting how far they are satisfied.
distinguish.testing.testcoveragetarget: the element identifies the endpoint, workflow or component in scope for testing, rather than its coverage metrics.

types.title: TargetInputField
types.description: A test-design association that binds one input field of a TestCoverageTarget's artifact (an API parameter, data-model property or UI input) to the InputSpacePartition used to divide that field into equivalence classes. It also records whether the field must appear in test inputs for that target. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are defining the equivalence classes of an input dimension itself, independent of which target or field uses them. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when you are stating which values of a partition a specific CoverageRequirement must exercise, rather than which partition governs a target's field. Use InputSelection instead when you are binding a concrete test datum to a partition value for an individual TestCaseSketch. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the symbol represents the endpoint, workflow or component under test as a whole, not one of its input fields.
evidence: A parameterized test (pytest.mark.parametrize, JUnit @ParameterizedTest/@MethodSource) whose parameter is named after one request field of the endpoint under test, with value sets grouped as valid/invalid/boundary.
A per-endpoint test-data map or fixture keyed by request field name (e.g. {"email": EMAIL_CASES, "age": AGE_BOUNDARIES}) that pairs each field with a reusable case list.
A property-based or schema-driven generator bound to a single DTO/OpenAPI parameter (Hypothesis st.builds field override, fast-check arbitrary, Schemathesis hook for one parameter).

distinguish.testing.inputspacepartition: you are defining the equivalence classes of an input dimension itself, independent of which target or field uses them.
distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: you are stating which values of a partition a specific CoverageRequirement must exercise, rather than which partition governs a target's field.
distinguish.testing.inputselection: you are binding a concrete test datum to a partition value for an individual TestCaseSketch.
distinguish.testing.testcoveragetarget: the symbol represents the endpoint, workflow or component under test as a whole, not one of its input fields.

types.title: TestCaseSketch
types.description: A single test case design that combines specific input selections (one chosen value per relevant partition), a context variation and an expected outcome category to exercise one CoverageRequirement of a TestCoverageTarget. It may remain unimplemented or be linked through source to the individual test function, parameterized row or scenario that realizes it. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states which partitions, contexts or outcomes must be covered (the criterion), rather than one specific combination chosen to satisfy it. Use InputSelection instead when the element is one field's binding of a partition representative to a concrete datum inside a test case, not the whole test case. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element lists which partition values a coverage requirement demands across all its tests, rather than the values one test case uses. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies the endpoint, component or workflow under test, which anchors many test cases, rather than an individual test case against it.
evidence: An individual test function or method (pytest test_*, Jest it()/test(), JUnit @Test) whose name, docstring or tag cites a requirement or partition, e.g. 'rejects quantity below zero'.
A single row of a parameterized test, such as a pytest.mark.parametrize id, a JUnit @CsvSource line or a Gherkin 'Scenario Outline' Examples row, binding concrete inputs to an expected result.
A test-case entry in a test plan, spreadsheet or test-management export (TestRail, Xray, Zephyr) with an ID, preconditions, input values, expected result and a status such as Draft or Approved.

distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: the element states which partitions, contexts or outcomes must be covered (the criterion), rather than one specific combination chosen to satisfy it.
distinguish.testing.inputselection: the element is one field's binding of a partition representative to a concrete datum inside a test case, not the whole test case.
distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the element lists which partition values a coverage requirement demands across all its tests, rather than the values one test case uses.
distinguish.testing.testcoveragetarget: the element identifies the endpoint, component or workflow under test, which anchors many test cases, rather than an individual test case against it.

types.title: TestCoverageModel
types.description: A versioned, application-scoped coverage specification that acts as the root container for the coverage targets, input partitions, context variations, coverage requirements, exclusions and test case sketches of exactly one application or API. It corresponds to a test plan as a whole, not to any individual target, test, suite or results report. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies one endpoint, workflow, UI component, job or integration flow that needs coverage, rather than the whole application's coverage specification. Use CoverageSummary instead when the element reports aggregated counts or status across a model's targets, requirements and sketches, rather than defining the coverage scope itself. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states the criteria (partitions, contexts, outcomes, coverage strategy) that a single target must satisfy, rather than containing all targets and requirements.
evidence: A top-level test plan or coverage manifest file (e.g. test-plan.yaml, coverage-model.json) carrying a version and an application or service identifier, and listing the endpoints or features to be tested.
A TEST_PLAN.md or docs/testing/plan document for one service that has 'Features to be tested', 'Approach' and 'Pass/fail criteria' sections.

A test-generation configuration that imports one OpenAPI document or application spec (e.g. a schemathesis, dredd or contract-test config pointing at openapi.yaml) and produces the set of coverage targets for that application.

distinguish.testing.testcoveragetarget: the element identifies one endpoint, workflow, UI component, job or integration flow that needs coverage, rather than the whole application's coverage specification.
distinguish.testing.coveragesummary: the element reports aggregated counts or status across a model's targets, requirements and sketches, rather than defining the coverage scope itself.
distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: the element states the criteria (partitions, contexts, outcomes, coverage strategy) that a single target must satisfy, rather than containing all targets and requirements.

types.title: TestCoverageTarget
types.description: A test-scope entry in a TestCoverageModel that names one production artifact or capability (an API operation, UI view, business workflow, data migration, integration flow, scheduled job, application component, data entity or library) whose behaviour must be verified. It is the anchor to which input fields, outcome categories, coverage requirements and test case sketches for that artifact attach. It records what is in scope, not the production code itself. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states the criteria (e.g. boundary-values, pairwise) that must be exercised for a target, rather than naming the thing to be tested. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element is an individual designed or implemented test case selecting specific partition values, rather than the artifact those cases exercise. Use TestCoverageModel instead when the element is the application-wide root aggregating many targets, partitions and requirements, rather than a single artifact in scope. Use TargetCoverageSummary instead when the element reports sketch, implemented or automated counts and a percentage for a target, rather than defining the target.
evidence: A test suite block (describe/class/@Nested) named after a specific endpoint, component, job or workflow, e.g. describe('POST /orders'), whose tests all import or call that one production symbol
A test plan, coverage manifest or traceability file (YAML/JSON/Markdown) listing 'features to be tested' entries keyed by operationId, route, component or job name, with a priority

Coverage tool configuration that scopes include patterns or thresholds to a named module, endpoint handler or scheduled-job entry point (e.g. per-path thresholds in jest/istanbul or a JaCoCo include rule)
